intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis-4 (FHL4) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding syntaxin-11 (STX11; 605014) on chromosome 6q24.

checks.claim: Familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis-4 (FHL4) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the STX11 gene, which encodes syntaxin-11.
checks.evidence_quote: we found homozygous mutations in STX11 in five consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindreds
checks.explanation: Paper reports only homozygous STX11 mutations; compound heterozygous mutations are not described.

checks.claim: The STX11 gene is located on chromosome 6q24.
checks.evidence_quote: Linkage to a 10 cM region on chromosome 6q24 between D6S1569 and D6S960 defined a novel FHL locus. By screening positional candidate genes, we identified a homozygous deletion of 5 bp in the syntaxin 11 gene (STX11)
checks.explanation: STX11 identified as positional candidate in the 6q24 region.

paragraphs.text: Familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis is an autosomal recessive immune disorder that usually begins in infancy or early childhood. Features include fever, hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, and infiltration of organs, including the central nervous system, by activated lymphocytes and histiocytes that show hemophagocytosis. Laboratory findings include hypertriglyceridemia, hypofibrinogenemia, and poor or absent natural killer (NK) cell cytotoxicity. FHL4 is the form caused by deficiency of syntaxin-11, a protein involved in cytotoxic granule exocytosis.

checks.claim: Familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis is an autosomal recessive immune disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (FHL) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by hyperactive phagocytes
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis usually begins in infancy or early childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: Familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (FHL) is an autosomal-recessive disease that affects young children.
checks.explanation: Abstract says it affects young children; 'usually begins in infancy or early childhood' is more specific.

checks.claim: Features of familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis include fever.
checks.evidence_quote: clinically diagnosed based on fulfillment of five out of eight criteria including fever, splenomegaly, bicytopenia, hypertriglyceridemia and/or hypofibrinogenemia
checks.explanation: Fever is listed among the HLH criteria.

checks.claim: Features of familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis include hepatosplenomegaly.
checks.evidence_quote: clinically diagnosed based on fulfillment of five out of eight criteria including fever, splenomegaly, bicytopenia
checks.explanation: Splenomegaly is a criterion and hepatomegaly appears in the patient table, but hepatosplenomegaly is not described as a general feature.

checks.claim: Features of familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis include cytopenias.
checks.evidence_quote: fever, splenomegaly, bicytopenia, hypertriglyceridemia and/or hypofibrinogenemia
checks.explanation: Bicytopenia is listed among the diagnostic criteria.

checks.claim: In familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, organs, including the central nervous system, are infiltrated by activated lymphocytes and histiocytes that show hemophagocytosis.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Organ/CNS infiltration not described; abstract only mentions hyperactive phagocytes.

checks.claim: Laboratory findings in familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis include hypertriglyceridemia.
checks.evidence_quote: fever, splenomegaly, bicytopenia, hypertriglyceridemia and/or hypofibrinogenemia, hemophagocytosis
checks.explanation: Hypertriglyceridemia is listed among the criteria.

checks.claim: Laboratory findings in familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis include hypofibrinogenemia.
checks.evidence_quote: fever, splenomegaly, bicytopenia, hypertriglyceridemia and/or hypofibrinogenemia, hemophagocytosis
checks.explanation: Hypofibrinogenemia is listed among the criteria.

checks.claim: Laboratory findings in familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis include poor or absent natural killer (NK) cell cytotoxicity.
checks.evidence_quote: hemophagocytosis, low/absent natural killer (NK) cell activity, hyperferritinemia
checks.explanation: Low or absent NK cell activity is listed among the criteria.

checks.claim: FHL4 is the form of familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis caused by deficiency of syntaxin-11.
checks.evidence_quote: We could demonstrate that syntaxin 11 protein was absent in the mononuclear cell fraction of patients with the homozygous 5 bp deletion.
checks.explanation: The title links FHL type 4 to STX11 mutations, and the abstract shows the protein is absent in patients.

checks.claim: Syntaxin-11 is a protein involved in cytotoxic granule exocytosis.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed binding of the N-terminal Habc domain of Stx11 to Munc18-2, stabilizing Stx11 expression, and facilitating cytotoxic lymphocyte exocytosis.
checks.explanation: Describes syntaxin-11's role in cytotoxic granule exocytosis.

paragraphs.text: Ohadi et al. (1999) used homozygosity mapping in consanguineous families of Kurdish origin with familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis and mapped the disease locus to chromosome 6q24. These families did not show linkage to the 9q or 10q loci reported earlier for FHL.

checks.claim: Ohadi et al. (1999) studied consanguineous families of Kurdish origin with familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Ohadi et al. (1999) is a different paper; this abstract does not describe it.

checks.claim: Ohadi et al. (1999) used homozygosity mapping to map the familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis locus in the Kurdish families to chromosome 6q24.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Ohadi et al. (1999) mapping is not described in this abstract.

checks.claim: The Kurdish families studied by Ohadi et al. (1999) did not show linkage to the 9q or 10q loci reported earlier for familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Exclusion of 9q/10q linkage not mentioned in this abstract.

paragraphs.text: Familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis is genetically heterogeneous. Other forms are caused by mutation in the perforin gene (FHL2), UNC13D (FHL3), and STXBP2 (FHL5). Another locus maps to chromosome 9q (FHL1).

checks.claim: Familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: mutations in the perforin 1 gene (PRF1) and in UNC13D are associated with FHL2 and FHL3, respectively, indicating genetic heterogeneity
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: FHL2 is caused by mutation in the perforin gene.
checks.evidence_quote: mutations in the perforin 1 gene (PRF1) and in UNC13D are associated with FHL2 and FHL3, respectively
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: FHL3 is caused by mutation in the UNC13D gene.
checks.evidence_quote: mutations in the perforin 1 gene (PRF1) and in UNC13D are associated with FHL2 and FHL3, respectively
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: FHL5 is caused by mutation in the STXBP2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: studies of how Munc18-2 mutations associated with FHL5 impact Stx11 binding
checks.explanation: Munc18-2 (encoded by STXBP2, per the paper) mutations are associated with FHL5.

checks.claim: The FHL1 locus maps to chromosome 9q.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. FHL1 locus on 9q not mentioned.

paragraphs.text: In consanguineous families of Kurdish/Turkish origin with FHL linked to 6q24, zur Stadt et al. (2005) narrowed the candidate region and identified homozygous mutations in the STX11 gene in affected individuals. The mutations included a large homozygous deletion that removes the STX11 coding sequence, as well as small frameshift mutations.

checks.claim: zur Stadt et al. (2005) studied consanguineous families of Kurdish/Turkish origin with familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis linked to chromosome 6q24.
checks.evidence_quote: We performed genome-wide homozygosity mapping in a large consanguineous Kurdish kindred with five children affected with FHL. Linkage to a 10 cM region on chromosome 6q24
checks.explanation: Linkage to 6q24 shown for the large Kurdish kindred; the additional Turkish/Kurdish families were identified by mutation screening, and their linkage is not stated.

checks.claim: zur Stadt et al. (2005) narrowed the 6q24 candidate region for familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.
checks.evidence_quote: Linkage to a 10 cM region on chromosome 6q24 between D6S1569 and D6S960 defined a novel FHL locus.
checks.explanation: Abstract describes defining a 10 cM region, not explicitly narrowing a previously reported region.

checks.claim: zur Stadt et al. (2005) identified homozygous STX11 mutations in affected individuals from the Kurdish/Turkish families with FHL.
checks.evidence_quote: we found homozygous mutations in STX11 in five consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindreds
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The STX11 mutations identified by zur Stadt et al. (2005) included a large homozygous deletion that removes the STX11 coding sequence.
checks.evidence_quote: one family with a large 19.2 kb genomic deletion spanning the entire coding region of STX11 (exon 2)
checks.explanation: The deletion spans the entire coding region and is homozygous.

checks.claim: The STX11 mutations identified by zur Stadt et al. (2005) included small frameshift mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: we identified a homozygous deletion of 5 bp in the syntaxin 11 gene (STX11) in this family
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a single recurrent 5-bp deletion, implicitly a frameshift but not called one, plus a nonsense mutation. It does not describe several small frameshift mutations.

paragraphs.text: Rudd et al. (2006) screened patients with HLH, most of them of Turkish origin, for STX11 mutations and found homozygous mutations in a subset. They reported that STX11 mutations were a common cause of FHL in Turkish patients, and that some patients with STX11 mutations had a milder or later-onset course than patients with perforin mutations.

checks.claim: Rudd et al. (2006) screened patients with HLH for STX11 mutations, most of them of Turkish origin.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutational analysis of STX11 by direct sequencing was done in 28 FHL families that did not harbour perforin mutations
checks.explanation: Screening of PRF1-negative FHL families is stated, but Turkish origin is not mentioned in the abstract.

checks.claim: Rudd et al. (2006) found homozygous STX11 mutations in a subset of the HLH patients screened.
checks.evidence_quote: affecting six of 34 children in four of 28 unrelated PRF1 negative families
checks.explanation: Mutations were found in a subset, but zygosity (homozygous) is not stated in the abstract.

checks.claim: Rudd et al. (2006) reported that STX11 mutations were a common cause of FHL in Turkish patients.
checks.explanation: Turkish patients are not mentioned. The abstract reports mutations in 14% of PRF1-negative families, not that STX11 mutations are a common cause in Turks.

checks.claim: Rudd et al. (2006) reported that some patients with STX11 mutations had a milder or later-onset course than patients with perforin mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Three patients experienced long periods (> or = 1 year) in remission without specific treatment, which is very uncommon in this disease. Despite the milder phenotype
checks.explanation: A milder phenotype is noted, but there is no explicit comparison with perforin-mutation patients and no mention of later onset.

paragraphs.text: Bryceson et al. (2007) found that NK cells from STX11-deficient patients could not degranulate when they encountered susceptible target cells, so their cytotoxicity was impaired. Stimulation of the NK cells with interleukin-2 partly restored degranulation and cytotoxicity. This suggested that syntaxin-11 is needed for cytotoxic granule exocytosis and that other components can partly compensate for its loss.

checks.claim: Bryceson et al. (2007) found that NK cells from STX11-deficient patients could not degranulate when they encountered susceptible target cells.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Bryceson et al. (2007) findings not in this paper.

checks.claim: Bryceson et al. (2007) found that NK cell cytotoxicity was impaired in STX11-deficient patients.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Bryceson et al. (2007) findings not in this paper.

checks.claim: Bryceson et al. (2007) found that stimulating NK cells from STX11-deficient patients with interleukin-2 partly restored degranulation and cytotoxicity.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. IL-2 restoration not described in this paper.

checks.claim: The findings of Bryceson et al. (2007) suggested that syntaxin-11 is needed for cytotoxic granule exocytosis.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Bryceson et al. (2007) conclusions not in this paper.

checks.claim: The findings of Bryceson et al. (2007) suggested that other components can partly compensate for loss of syntaxin-11.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Not addressed in this paper.

paragraphs.text: Stx11-deficient mice had defective degranulation of cytotoxic lymphocytes. After infection with lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus they developed an HLH-like disease, which was reported to be milder than that of perforin-deficient mice (D'Orlando et al., 2013; Kogl et al., 2013).

checks.claim: Stx11-deficient mice had defective degranulation of cytotoxic lymphocytes.
checks.evidence_quote: Although syntaxin-11 (Stx11)-deficiency abrogates degranulation by both cytotoxic T cells and NK cells.
checks.explanation: States that Stx11 deficiency abrogates degranulation, but does not specify mice.

checks.claim: Stx11-deficient mice developed an HLH-like disease after infection with lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Mouse LCMV infection not described in this abstract.

checks.claim: The HLH-like disease in Stx11-deficient mice infected with lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus was reported to be milder than that of perforin-deficient mice.
checks.evidence_quote: Relative to other FHL subtypes, patients with STX11 non-sense mutations or Stx11-deficient mice typically display less severe disease.
checks.explanation: Milder disease in Stx11-deficient mice is stated relative to other FHL subtypes; no specific comparison with perforin-deficient mice or LCMV.
